title: Employees' rights and responsibilities
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:11Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-rights-responsibilities, teaches only the general idea of rights and responsibilities with consumer examples, while the new point names specific workplace rights (safety, freedom from discrimination and harassment) and duties (working safely, following lawful instructions), so it needs new content rather than small changes.

draft.title: Employees' rights and responsibilities
card: Employees have the right to a safe workplace. They can raise safety concerns without being punished for it.
Employees also have the right to work free of discrimination and harassment. Discrimination is unfair treatment because of a trait such as race, sex, age or disability.
Employees must work safely. They must follow safety rules, use equipment correctly and take care not to put others at risk.
Employees must also follow lawful instructions from their employer. An instruction to break the law, or to do something unsafe, is not one they must follow.
draft.remember: Employees have the right to safety and fair treatment, and must work safely and follow lawful instructions.

a.q: Jai works in a warehouse in Penrith. Which of these is his responsibility as an employee?
opts: Wearing the safety boots supplied for the job
Being paid the rate set for his work
Working in a place free of harassment
Raising a safety concern without being punished
a.why: Using the safety equipment supplied is part of working safely, which is a duty of employees. The other three are rights Jai holds, not things he must do.
a.clue: Three options are things Jai is owed. One is something he must do.

b.q: A café owner in Orange tells a waiter to serve a customer, then tells him to lift a heavy machine alone, which a safety rule forbids. What should the waiter do?
opts: Follow the first instruction but not the unsafe one
Follow both, because bosses decide the tasks
Refuse both, because instructions are optional
Follow neither until he is paid extra
b.why: Employees must follow lawful instructions, and serving a customer is one. An instruction that breaks a safety rule is not one they must follow, so refusing both is wrong.
b.clue: Check each instruction separately: is it lawful and safe?

a.best: Wearing the safety boots supplied for the job

b.best: Follow the first instruction but not the unsafe one
